主要内容: The Walt Disney Company replaced its existing $1.5 billion 364-Day Credit Agreement and $2.25 billion Five-Year Credit Agreement with new facilities. The new $1.5 billion 364-Day facility will expire on March 10, 2017, and the new $2.25 billion Five-Year facility will expire in March 2021. Under both new facilities, the company has the option to borrow at LIBOR-based rates plus a spread, subject to a cap and a floor that vary with its debt rating. The remaining provisions of each new facility, including representations, warranties, covenants, and events of default, are substantially similar to the former facilities. Each new facility contains only one financial covenant, relating to interest coverage, and excludes certain entities, including Euro Disney, Hong Kong Disneyland, and Shanghai Disney Resort, from any representations, covenants, or events of default. Copies of the new agreements are filed as Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2, respectively, and are incorporated by reference into this report. The changes reflect the company's ongoing efforts to manage its debt obligations and financial flexibility.
